title: Annual return and reconciliation
learn: Why audited turnover and GST turnover differ, line by line
How the credit in the books ties to the year’s 3Bs
What to do with a supply that no return shows
do: Classify seven turnover papers and five credit items
Build the bridge for GSTR-9 and 9C

case.client: Tamhini Drivetech Private Limited, a Chakan company that makes gears, shafts and hubs for vehicle makers, with a depot at Hosur in Tamil Nadu
case.team: Neethu Thomas (GST senior) and Varun Shetty, who has Hosur’s return; at Tamhini, Pallavi Shinde sends the data and Mahesh Kadam, the accounts head, approves payments
case.goal: Bridge Chakan’s 2026–27 turnover and input tax credit from the audited accounts to its returns, explain every difference and find what the returns missed, before GSTR-9 and 9C are filed.
case.period: Year ended 31 March 2027 · annual return due 31 December 2027
case.where: Firm office, Prabhat Road · Wednesday 1 to Friday 3 December 2027

messages: Chakan’s 2026–27 annual return is ours; Varun has Hosur’s. Start from the audited revenue and the input ledgers and walk to what Chakan’s returns show.
Every difference needs a reason or a payment. The bridge to me by Friday; we file well before the 31st.

body: Annual return data for 2026–27 attached: sales by GSTIN, the stock transfer, export and scrap registers, the input ledgers and the fixed asset register, all after the audit entries. On the points your team asked about:
- Credit note 001 to Ashvaratha Motors (28 March, price reduction on input shaft 1142 for January–March) is in the March books. We uploaded it with the April 2027 GSTR-1.
- Naik’s invoice 0412 of 31 March is in the March GSTR-1, and its GST went with March’s 3B. Your audit team moved the sale to April (AJE-1). Should we cut 2026–27 turnover in GSTR-9 to match?
- Kharun’s bill of 29 March was booked in March and its credit taken in March’s 3B, filed on 20 April. The audit moved it to April (AJE-8), so I think we should reverse the ₹3,35,520 in GSTR-9.
- Rankala’s bill of 31 March was entered on 1 April and its credit taken in the April 2027 3B. The audit brought it back into March (AJE-6).
- The old lathe went to Bilal Ferrous Traders on 14 December. It was sold as scrap, so plant did not ask for an invoice; the ₹45,000 came by NEFT.
- The service centre bill for MD sir’s car (February, GST ₹6,840) shows in 2B. We booked the GST to vehicle running and took no credit.

tasks.title: Turnover: accounts to returns
tasks.prompt: Walk from the audited revenue to what Chakan’s 2026–27 GSTR-1s show. For each paper, say what it does to the accounts figure and why. Pallavi’s mail, the revenue note, Varun’s sheet and the registrations file are under Other papers. Your calls go to Neethu when you move on.

hints: Same two questions as October’s tie-up, now for the whole year: is it in the audited revenue, and is it in Chakan’s GSTR-1s? Only a yes and a no make a difference.
The revenue bridge can’t see what is in neither. Look at what left the company outside revenue.

items.label: Hosur depot’s sales
items.note: Take Hosur out first. The depot bills on its own Tamil Nadu GSTIN and files its own GSTR-9 and 9C; Varun has that one. Chakan’s bridge starts at ₹98,76,20,000.

items.label: Exports to Kenya under LUT
items.note: No difference. Exports under the LUT carry no tax, but they are still in Chakan’s GSTR-1, under exports, and in its turnover, just as they are in revenue. No tax doesn’t mean no reporting.

items.label: Naik Auto Spares · invoice 0412 of 31 March
items.note: Add. The invoice was issued on 31 March, so its GST belongs to March and was paid. The audit moved only the revenue to April, because the goods left on 2 April. Nothing to undo in the returns.

items.label: Old lathe sold on 14 December
items.note: In no return. A business asset sold for ₹45,000 is a supply, scrap or not, and Bilal got no invoice. Only the profit sits in other income, so the revenue bridge can’t show it; the asset register does. Tax to pay.

items.label: Stock transfers to the Hosur depot
items.note: Add. Goods sent to Tamhini’s own Hosur GSTIN are a supply between distinct persons, invoiced with IGST and in Chakan’s GSTR-1, but they never touch a sales ledger.

items.label: Scrap sales to Bilal Ferrous
items.note: No difference. Every load went to Bilal on a TD/SC tax invoice, sits in revenue from operations and is in GSTR-1. The bridge moves only what is in one and not the other.

items.label: Ashvaratha Motors · credit note 001 of 28 March
items.note: Add. The credit note cut March’s revenue, but it was uploaded with April 2027’s GSTR-1, so the year’s GSTR-1s don’t have it. In GSTR-9 it goes in the part for this year’s items declared in next year’s returns.

tasks.title: Credit: books to returns
tasks.prompt: Now the credit: from the input ledgers in the audited books to the credit Chakan’s 2026–27 3Bs took. For each item, say where it sits. The input ledgers, Varun’s sheet, the audit adjustments and Pallavi’s mail are under Other papers. Your calls go to Neethu when you move on.

lockOnLeave.ask: Hand your credit calls to Neethu?
lockOnLeave.note: You can’t change them after this.
lockOnLeave.done: Handed to Neethu. You can read your calls but not change them.

hints: Same two questions: is it in Chakan’s books for 2026–27, and in a 2026–27 3B? Two audit entries moved bills across 31 March, one each way.

options.label: 3B first: this year’s 3B, next year’s books
Books first: this year’s books, next year’s 3B

fields.label: Your note for the file
fields.placeholder: For example: claimed in July’s 3B; booked in July

items.label: Hosur depot’s input ledgers
items.note: Take them out. That IGST is the tax on Chakan’s transfer invoices, which Hosur claims, and the CGST and SGST are on the depot rent. Hosur’s 9C explains them; Chakan’s starts at ₹16,04,17,208.

items.label: Reverse charge on legal fees
items.note: No difference. Tamhini paid the tax on its legal fees in cash and took the same ₹43,200 as credit in those 3Bs; the books carry exactly that.

items.label: Kharun Steels · bill of 29 March
items.note: In March’s 3B, out of the 2026–27 books: the steel came in on 2 April, so the audit moved the bill to April. One claim, in a different year from the books: timing. Watch for a second claim.

items.label: Service centre bill · MD’s car
items.note: No difference. Repairs of a car like the MD’s are blocked credit, so the ₹6,840 went to vehicle running: it is in neither the input ledgers nor the 3Bs’ net credit. A bill showing in 2B doesn’t make its credit claimable.

items.label: Rankala Forgings · bill of 31 March
items.note: Kharun the other way round. The blanks came in at 7:40 pm on 31 March, so the audit put the bill in March; the credit went in April 2027’s 3B, inside the time limit. Timing again.

tasks.title: Build the bridge
tasks.prompt: Put your calls into figures. Enter each line as it moves the accounts figure, minus to take out and plus to add, then each total; both should equal Varun’s sheet. Last, the lathe: its value and 18% GST on that value; the deal had no GST in it, so the tax goes on top.

lockOnLeave.note: You can’t change it after this.
lockOnLeave.done: Handed to Neethu. You can read your bridge but not change it.

tasks.title: Write to Mahesh
tasks.prompt: Mahesh approves every payment, so he needs one mail from us: what the bridge found and what Tamhini does next. Pick the right line for each point.
hints: GSTR-9 can’t be revised and gives no new credit, and after 30 November a 2026–27 supply can’t go into a GSTR-1.

options.text: Turnover: Chakan’s 2026–27 GSTR-1s come to ₹1,17,75,97,000 against audited revenue of ₹1,18,33,40,000, and the whole gap is explained: Hosur’s ₹19,57,20,000 goes in Hosur’s own return, and the transfers to Hosur, Naik’s 31 March invoice and Ashvaratha’s credit note make up the rest.
options.why: Every line has a paper and a reason, and no part of the gap is left for the department to ask about.

options.text: Turnover: Chakan’s 2026–27 GSTR-1s come to ₹1,17,75,97,000 against audited revenue of ₹1,18,33,40,000. Since the audit moved Naik’s 31 March sale to April, we will cut ₹46,80,000 from 2026–27 turnover in GSTR-9, so that the return matches your audited accounts for the year exactly.
options.why: The invoice was issued on 31 March, so the supply and its GST stay in 2026–27. The audit moved the revenue, not the invoice.

options.text: Turnover: Chakan’s 2026–27 GSTR-1s come to ₹1,17,75,97,000 against audited revenue of ₹1,18,33,40,000. The transfers to Hosur are only stock moving between your own two units, so we will show their ₹18,40,57,000 in 9C as unreconciled and explain it to the department later.
options.why: Transfers to Tamhini’s own Tamil Nadu GSTIN are supplies between distinct persons. They are a reason, not an unreconciled gap.

options.text: Lathe: the 2008 lathe sold to Bilal Ferrous Traders on 14 December 2026 for ₹45,000 went out without a tax invoice. Please raise the invoice now so we can put it in this month’s GSTR-1, and approve the ₹8,100 of GST, with interest, for this month’s 3B.
options.why: Too late for that: a 2026–27 supply can’t go into a GSTR-1 after 30 November 2027.

options.text: Lathe: the 2008 lathe sold to Bilal Ferrous Traders on 14 December 2026 for ₹45,000 went out without a tax invoice. A business asset sold is a supply, so we will declare it in GSTR-9. Please approve the ₹8,100 of GST, with interest, for DRC-03 in cash.
options.why: With 30 November gone, GSTR-9 and DRC-03 are the route, and that payment can only come from the cash ledger.

options.text: Lathe: the 2008 lathe sold to Bilal Ferrous Traders on 14 December 2026 for ₹45,000 went out without a tax invoice. It went out as scrap, so no GST applies to it, and we will leave it out of both GSTR-9 and 9C, as the plant treated it.
options.why: Scrap is taxable: Tamhini bills Bilal GST on every load of turnings. A business asset sold for a price is a supply, whatever state it is in.

options.text: Credit: Chakan’s books and 3Bs differ only by timing. As the audit moved Kharun’s bill to April, we will reverse its ₹3,35,520 in GSTR-9, and as Rankala’s bill is now in the March books, we will claim its ₹8,900 in the same return.
options.why: GSTR-9 gives no new credit, and Rankala’s was taken in April’s 3B anyway. Kharun’s was taken once; reversing it now would lose it, with 30 November gone.

options.text: Credit: Chakan’s books and 3Bs differ only by timing. Kharun’s ₹3,35,520 now sits in your April books, so it can be claimed again in this month’s 3B; Rankala’s ₹8,900 went in April’s 3B and needs no further step from us.
options.why: That would be Kharun’s credit twice: March’s 3B already took it.

options.text: Credit: Chakan’s books and 3Bs differ only by timing. Kharun’s ₹3,35,520 went in March’s 3B and the audit moved the bill to April; Rankala’s ₹8,900 went the other way. Please confirm no 2027–28 return took Kharun’s credit again.
options.why: Each bill was claimed once, in a different year from its books. The check now is for a second claim.

freeText.label: Your own line for the mail

wrap.text: Every difference had its paper: four on the turnover, three on the credit. The lathe is the one that costs money: ₹8,100 and its interest now, rather than after a notice. I’ll take Mahesh through your mail this afternoon.

wrapPartial.text: The bridge is Hosur out; the transfers, Naik and the credit note in; two timing items on the credit. The lathe is in no return, so it is tax to pay. Redo your misses below before the mail goes to Mahesh; I don’t file a bridge that doesn’t tie.

wrapRetry.text: Two questions for every paper: is it in the audited revenue, and is it in Chakan’s GSTR-1s? A yes and a no is a difference. Then look outside revenue, at the asset register, for anything sold without an invoice.

passNeeds.note: You need half the turnover marks to pass; the lathe counts three times. The bridge starts there.

model.intro: Chakan’s returns follow its own GSTIN and its invoices; the audited accounts follow the whole company and its sales. Take Hosur’s sales and credit out, add what Chakan’s GSTR-1s carry and its revenue does not, and the turnover ties to the rupee; the credit ties after two timing items. The lathe is in no return at all, so it is tax to pay.

principles: Book turnover and GST turnover measure different things; the bridge names each difference and the paper behind it.
A taxable supply that no return carries, like an asset sold without an invoice, is tax to pay.
GSTR-9 can’t be revised and gives no new credit, so give every difference a reason or a payment before filing.

interview.q: What is the difference between GSTR-9 and GSTR-9C?
interview.checking: Whether you know who files what, and that 9C is now self-certified.
outline: GSTR-9 is each GSTIN’s annual return, filled mostly from that year’s GSTR-1s and 3Bs; due 31 December.
GSTR-9C reconciles it with the audited accounts; it is self-certified, needed above ₹5 crore aggregate turnover.
GSTR-9 can’t be revised, so the bridge comes first[[; in the simulation I traced {t} turnover {t|difference|differences}]].

interview.q: Why would turnover in the audited accounts differ from GST turnover?
interview.checking: Whether you can name real reasons, each with an example, not textbook guesses.
outline: The accounts cover the company; GST runs per GSTIN, so in the simulation the depot’s sales came out.
Transfers to its other GSTIN were supplies, not revenue; an audit entry moved a sale, not its invoice.
A taxable supply in no return is tax to pay[[: I found a lathe sold without an invoice{lathe|}]].
